test_command: dotnet build api/Biolog.Api/Biolog.Api.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.IntegrationTests/Biolog.IntegrationTests.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.UnitTests/Biolog.UnitTests.csproj && bash scripts/check-module-project-references.sh && python3 scripts/check-contract-freeze.py && bash scripts/secret-scan.sh && (cd web && npx tsc --noEmit)
notes:
Post-acceptance TD-style fix on an already-DONE story (same pattern TD-WEB-PROVENANCE-BRIDGE-REVERIFY established for BIO-TEN-003): no automation/biolog.py verb re-stamps builder_commit from DONE (late-commit requires READY_FOR_REVIEW/READY_FOR_ACCEPTANCE, builder-complete requires BUILDING/ASSIGNED/CHANGES_REQUIRED - both confirmed by running late-commit first and reading its actual refusal, not assumed), so this fix is committed directly on feature/BIO-TEN-002 and tracked via this new evidence file rather than the usual start/builder-complete cycle.

BIO-OPS-002's acceptance review BLOCKED on two High findings against api/Biolog.Api/Tenancy/ (the demo-session bridge this story has historically extended directly - BIO-TEN-002-QA-01/QA-03 commits touch these exact host-level files, not just api/features/bio-ten-002/**), not BIO-IDN-006 (RBAC) or BIO-TEN-003 (tenant feature configuration), the other two stories god asked to check.

OPS002-F01 (High): DemoSessionTenantResolver always resolved to the ONE configured WebSessionBridge:SyntheticTenantId regardless of the verified token's own tenantId claim (alpha/beta), so the shell's tenant selector never changed backend tenant/repository/permission context - AC01 was cosmetic. Fixed: TryVerify (TryResolve is now a thin wrapper over it) maps the claim through a two-entry allowlist - alpha keeps using the original SyntheticTenantId unchanged, beta uses the new optional WebSessionBridge:SyntheticTenantIdBeta, falling back to alpha's tenant when unconfigured. Purely additive/opt-in: every existing demo-bridge story (BIO-PHO-003/BIO-TRN-003/BIO-ATT-003/BIO-DEV-004/BIO-TEN-003's own reverify) that only configures the primary key keeps working identically, confirmed by the full zero-regression integration run.

Tried and reverted: seeding DemoSessionIdentitySeed's three fixed demo identities into beta too, for symmetry. Caught by this fix's own new tests (not a reviewer) before it could ship: InMemoryPersonRepository keys Person rows by Person.Id ALONE (a single, process-lifetime, cross-tenant dictionary, confirmed by reading its own header/implementation), so creating the 'same' person id under a second tenant threw a genuine person_id_collision. Minting distinct beta-only person ids would dodge the collision but the web side's deriveDemoActorId(roleId) is deliberately tenant-agnostic, so those identities would never actually be reachable without a second, tenant-aware actor-derivation mechanism on the web side - well beyond these two findings' own scope. Reverted to the original single-tenant seeding; beta is a genuinely separate, currently-empty tenant when configured, which is still a real AC01 data-context change and arguably a stronger AC02 isolation proof than a seeded-but-unreachable design.

OPS002-F02 (High): startDemoSession revoked/reissued the session token but called no audit API; no backend endpoint or sink for a tenant/role context-change audit record existed anywhere, so AC04 had nothing to accept. Fixed: new POST /api/v1/tenancy/demo-session/context-change (api/Biolog.Api/Tenancy/DemoSessionContextAuditEndpoints.cs), backed by a dedicated DemoSessionContextAuditEvent/IDemoSessionContextAuditSink/InMemoryDemoSessionContextAuditSink (own typed event, matching this codebase's established per-feature convention rather than overloading the narrower Biolog.Api.Audit.AuditEvent). Authorization is the demo session token itself via DemoSessionTenantResolver.TryVerify, deliberately NOT a second ActorProvenanceGate or a permission check - re-derived from first principles (ADR-0006, applying the ZB-INT005-01/02 lesson of re-justifying every route's own actual requirement) and disclosed in the endpoint's own header why neither would add a real boundary for this self-service demo mechanism. web/context/session-actions.ts's startDemoSession now calls this endpoint directly via BIOLOG_API_BASE_URL (the same base URL next.config.mjs's own rewrites() already uses) right after issuing the new token, passing the OLD claims it already verified moments earlier before revoking them. Deliberately best-effort/fire-and-forget (disclosed deviation from ADR-0003 Decision 1's usual hard-dependency rule): most of this app's own test suite runs the web app with no live backend at all, and making this a hard gate would break BIO-UX-002's own already-approved tenant/role switcher in every such run.

Verification: dotnet build clean (0 warnings/errors). New tests/dotnet/Biolog.IntegrationTests/DemoSessionContextAuditEndpointsTests.cs: 8/8 (alpha/beta resolve to genuinely different tenants; beta falls back to alpha's tenant when unconfigured; no-token/tampered-token rejected; partial/invalid previous-context rejected; initial-session and full-previous-context accepted). Full Biolog.IntegrationTests 288/288 (was 280, +8 new, zero regression elsewhere - this worktree had to merge develop in first, 1041 commits behind since its own acceptance, to pick up TD-WEB-PROVENANCE-BRIDGE's demo-session mechanism at all). Biolog.UnitTests 210/210 unchanged. scripts/check-module-project-references.sh PASS. scripts/check-contract-freeze.py PASS (39 artifacts, 83 future stories). scripts/secret-scan.sh clean. web tsc --noEmit clean (no new type errors; this worktree had no node_modules installed before this fix, confirmed pre-existing - npm install run once to make tsc runnable). No Playwright re-run: the only web change (session-actions.ts) is a server-side, fire-and-forget side effect behind an existing, already-approved UI control, with no new UI surface for any existing spec to observe.
